#3651. Five Race-Day Smartwatch Hacks Every Marathon Runner Should Know

I love my Garmin Forerunner 970, but the fact is, most runners don't need all the features it has to offer. In fact, for most road races, you can get by with whatever smartwatch you already own—as long as you know how to use it. If you've got a marathon or half-marathon coming up, these five tricks will only take a few minutes to set up, and they can save you from one of many of the small-but-avoidable disasters that can derail a good race.

Nothing spikes pre-race anxiety like standing in a corral of hundreds of people watching your watch fail to latch onto a signal. Tall buildings, crowded starts, and a sea of other devices make the first minute of GPS unreliable, which can leave your opening mileage pace wildly off.

The fix is simple: start the GPS search early. Step outside, into the open, as soon as you've dropped your bag, and select your run activity at least 10 to 15 minutes before the starting gun. If your watch supports multi-band or dual-frequency GPS, turn it on in the activity settings, since it's noticeably better in dense downtown starts. Then, don't press start until the gun goes off (or you cross the line, if you want chip-accurate pacing).

Bonus tip: If you're in a start corral with a long wait, you can lock the signal and then pause the activity screen. Just remember to hit start when you actually take off.

Multiple data screens are great for training, but overwhelming during a race. Too many numbers invite overthinking, and seeing the "wrong" number at mile two can lead you into a very stressful mile ten.

My recommendation is to build a dedicated race screen with three to four fields at most:

Lap pace or average lap pace (not instant pace, which jumps around constantly with GPS)

Distance or lap distance, so you know where you are relative to the mile markers

Heart rate, especially in the early miles when adrenaline tempts you to go out too fast

Elapsed time, for splits against your goal

Keep it clean and stripped down, and avoid the temptation to add cadence, power, vertical oscillation, and everything else. You can always review those stats during your cool-down.

A text from your boss at mile 14 is nobody's idea of a good time. Before race day, switch your watch to Do Not Disturb or Airplane mode, or turn on a dedicated activity mode that blocks notifications. This also saves battery, which matters if your marathon is going to take you four-plus hours.

After blocking the outside world, you can set race-specific alerts, like a high heart-rate alert to keep you honest in the first half. I also know runners who set a recurring time or distance alert for fueling—say, every 30 to 40 minutes, or every 5 miles—so remembering to down a gel or a sports drink doesn't depend on your fading brain.

Here's one thing I learn the hard way, every time: Your watch will almost always say you've run farther than the race course says you have. Race courses are measured along the shortest possible route, but along the way, you'll weave around people, take wide turns, and generally add extra distance. I've run marathons where my watch reads closer to 26.6 miles (nearly an extra half mile), so my "on pace" watch is actually behind my chip time.

The hack: Ignore the watch's auto-lap and press the lap button manually at each mile marker (or at every kilometer marker, if that's what the course uses). This gives you pace data aligned to the official course, not the satellite's best guess. It also gives you a quick mental check against your plan. If you've set up your watch for it, display average lap pace, then glance at it a few hundred meters after each marker to see how you're tracking. And don't panic if your watch beeps for a mile before you pass the marker—trust the course and your lap presses, and do your best to ignore the mismatched distance adding up.

Rain, sweat, high-fives, and a hasty cup grab at an aid station can all trigger accidental taps on a touchscreen watch. Few things are worse than discovering at mile 18 that you accidentally paused, ended, or switched screens on your activity. So before the race, turn on your watch's screen lock, so a stray touch doesn't do anything.

If your watch has a configurable wake gesture, consider turning it off to save battery, and set the backlight to a short timeout. While we're talking watch-wearing protocol, remember to wear it snugly, one finger-width above your wrist bone, for a better heart-rate reading as you sweat. Finally, if your watch has one, use the post-race auto-save reminder. (Otherwise, do your best to hit stop after you cross the finish line.)

Again, you don't need the most premium running-specific watch ahead of race day. If you have time, test these hacks on a long run, so that you're not wasting any precious mental energy during the big day.

#3650. Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something new. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

"The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)"

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's important is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people."

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

Rick Devens has simple advice for those who want to be on reality television, and for anyone who wants to be on the best reality shows, I'd listen up. Apparently the key to getting in the position to win Big Brother, or make wild moves on Survivor, is to be bold... even if you look foolish.

While we've seen people win Big Brother and Survivor by playing the middle, the most memorable winners and players are the ones who make the big moves. Other reality stars may suggest being chill, but not Devens. He told The Observer the key to his moves is this:

I think that's some universal advice most reality stars would give, which is why they were put on TV to begin with. Casting directors don't seek out people who will strive to worry about every move that's on camera, what could go wrong, or make rash decisions.

Rick Devens just won Big Brother, so he's a great person to ask this question. Not many people get the chance to play on both BB and Survivor, so those should continue to listen when it comes to why it's important to be fearless. As he continued:

You’re going to handicap yourself. You’re going to keep yourself from doing amazing things and having the most fun. Just go for it. Be fearless.

All this to say, not every person on reality television is Rick Devens. He's speaking with the bias of someone who was put on Survivor initially and welcomed back because of how he played. It's that same fearlessness that got him on Big Brother, hoping that "Chaos Devens" would be activated.

There's been some debate of whether Devens played as fast and loose on BB as he did on Survivor. Coming in the game with built-in allies in Dee Valladares and Angela Murray, as well as being voted to receive powers, certainly allowed him some freedom to make moves that other Houseguests weren't afforded. I would imagine that if any of those other Houseguests had been given those big of powers, they would've also jumped on the opportunity.

Rick Devens and Big Brother's producers, for that matter, would argue he and the icons had the biggest targets on their backs going into the game. The advantages allowed them to "even the odds" and prevent being targeted from the jump and being sent out of the game immediately. Neither had pointed out that former winner Rachel Reilly played in the previous season with only one week of safety as an advantage, but I digress.

In any case, Rick and the Icons playing Big Brother again resulted in big ratings for the series and a two-season renewal. Bringing in the viewers will also work a lot toward getting someone back on reality television, so I'm just waiting to see if we'll see him again if Season 30 of BB does end up being an all-star season. In the meantime, I'll enjoy all his previous reality TV appearances on Paramount+.

#3648. We Tested How Long It Takes To Run Out Of Gas In GTA 6

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive game! It takes about an hour and a half to sprint across the map. But most players will be driving around Vice City, and this time around, GTA 6 demands that you monitor your gas tank while cruising the streets and highways of Leonida. So how long before you need to fill up in GTA 6, and does it get annoying?

To test this out, I booted up Grand Theft Auto 6 and hopped into two different cars. First, I tested a basic and somewhat older pickup truck. I found a loop of highway near the southern part of Vice City and filled up my gas tank at a local station. Then, the journey began. For this test, I drove around like I normally do in GTA 6 when not being shot at or racing someone. I also tried really hard not to stop, but traffic is traffic, and sometimes I had to slow down or completely brake. I wanted to avoid damaging the engines of any vehicles during testing so as not to toss in yet another variable.

It took 29 minutes and 8 seconds for the pickup to run out of gas completely.

To provide some context: You can drive across the entire map of GTA 6 via its highways and with a lead foot in under 15 minutes. So, in theory, I think I could drive across the map twice before running out of gas.

For my next test, I swapped out the older pickup truck for a Banshee, a fast-as-heck sports car that has been a part of the franchise since at least GTA 3. I loaded up the gas tank and hit the same highway loop as before. I went faster in the Banshee, of course, but still avoided crashing and stopping as much as possible. I may have had to restart the test at one point when I slammed into a minivan and basically blew up my engine. Science is dangerous.

In GTA 6, while driving a Banshee sports car, it took 18 minutes and 31 seconds to drain my tank entirely.

So, assuming I don’t hit a minivan again, that’s enough time to drive across the entire map via highways and still have some fuel left over to get to a nearby station and fill up.

Finally, I grabbed an electric car modeled after a Tesla 3, found a nearby charging station, got the battery juiced up, and hit that same highway loop one more time. Luckily, I didn’t crash at all during this test, and after following the same rules as before, it took 20 minutes and 23 seconds.

Personally, across over 130 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I only ran out of gas once, not counting these tests. I ran out of battery once as well. In both cases they were stolen cars that didn’t have full tanks and I was too busy dodging cops to notice I was running out of go-go juice or zoom liquid. I also had a few moments where I got low on gas during getaways and had to change plans or vehicles to accommodate.

But for the most part, I forgot vehicles needed fuel when playing GTA 6. And the game does a good job of letting you know when you hit halfway and when you’re nearing empty, even marking the nearest station on the compass to help you get fueled up ASAP. There are also a lot of gas stations around, so I was rarely too far away to reach one. Also, if I was driving a personal vehicle that I owned, I could just use the in-game Scooter Bros app to request another one of my vehicles. And when, a bit later, I summoned back the car in which I’d run low on gas via that same app, it would have some extra fuel in the tank. Nifty.

So I never found the fuel tank (or battery management) annoying at all. In the early hours, when money is tight and car options are limited, it proved a bit more of a hassle. But later on, it stopped being a problem. If anything, it added a fun variable that could derail a robbery if I wasn’t being careful or cause me to ditch a stolen car for another option. I doubt it will cause most players too much annoyance.

The Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 robot vacuum and mop is down to $799.99 from $1,299.99 in an early Black Friday deal, saving you $500 and bringing it to its lowest price to date. Much of its appeal comes from a slim 3.1-inch profile that lets it reach under beds, sofas, and other low furniture where taller robot vacuums often can’t fit. #3646. Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

"If it's a war story, sure, it can be COD."

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold new directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

This latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty."

This isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

Even the best reality TV shows can be accused of being scripted, and while not every claim is substantiated, there are a lot of allegations. Personally, like many others, I might be taken aback on the off chance that such a claim turns out to be true. Just recently, I found two stories from people who allegedly got a first-hand look at the inner workings of America's Got Talent and Bar Rescue, and they're fascinating to read.

AGT regularly draws claims online, with people alleging that it's scripted or faking parts of its programming. This latest claim from Reddit comes from someone who allegedly worked on the set and took issue with how one contestant's story was edited in the episode. Take a read:

I worked on America's Got Talent's 7th season and I never watched the show before working on it. I spent 4 days working, interviewing talented people with a camera crew and producer. I will not forget, we interviewed this one older woman who was a drummer. She was vibrant and friendly and we had a great talk, and then I watched when the episode aired and they recut the interview to make her seem flighty and mentally... off. Then she goes out on stage in front of the country for Sharon Osborne to mock her. It was bad, it was heartbreaking, that this woman's crime was 'older than 40 and good at drums' and the people making that show took liberty to destroy her on a national platform. They asked me to work on season 8 and I turned them down without a conversation.

It's not uncommon for reality TV show subjects to complain about receiving unflattering or dishonest edits. Over the years, stars have alleged that producers can get the response they want out of them and then edit the footage to make it appear they said something entirely different from what they meant. If AGT actually engaged in this, it wouldn't be different from claims against many other shows on the 2026 TV schedule. Regardless, this should be a gentle reminder for viewers not to believe everything they see.

The thread also revealed someone who was pretty upset with Bar Rescue after the show allegedly "ruined" one of his favorite locales. The renovation show is wildly popular and entertaining, but that doesn't always mean it's tackling bars that are in trouble. On that note, per the aforementioned user, his go-to bar didn't even need to be rescued:

This bar was packed ALL THE TIME. You drive by at 3 PM on a Tuesday, packed. 2 PM on a Sunday, packed. On more than one occasion, we had gone to the bar on a Friday or Saturday to find no place to sit because it was so full. They even bought the space next to them and knocked out a wall to make more room...Then we heard that Bar Rescue was coming. We wondered why they would need to 'rescue' this bar that was always full of people. But we got excited to see our bar on TV.

From there, the writer claimed the bar's owners removed all the furniture and revamped the menu with new cocktails. His wife apparently stood in line to attend the reopening and was instructed before entering that she could only order the signature cocktail.

When the Bar Rescue episode aired, it pushed the narrative that the cocktails were super popular and that "no one wants beer." As mentioned, attendees were allegedly told they could only purchase cocktails, which made it seem like the show's producers decided that would be the story before filming ever began. In the end, the "rescue" ended up ruining the bar, at least in this person's opinion:

People stopped going. Last time I went, it was a Friday night, and there were like 6 other people in the place. The bar ended up moving locations, and now I don't have a neighborhood place anymore. Fuck Bar Rescue.

The whole account really makes me rethink the times I've seen Jon Taffer give advice on how to fix a bar. Of course, this is all alleged, and it's not like there are receipts or concrete proof of these claims. It isn't necessarily hard to believe, but given the lack of hard evidence or even any identifiable information, I'd take it with a grain of salt.

While America's Got Talent and Bar Rescue aren't the only reality television shows accused of scripting their unscripted moments, they are two established legacy shows. I'm sure they won't be the last shows to be accused of being deceptive to the audience watching at home, but I'm not sure it'll actually keep anyone from watching.

The 2026 TV schedule is winding down, but there is still lots of good TV to watch. Even if it is reality television, there's no shortage of entertainment as we close out the year.

#3643. After Finishing GTA 6, I Can Confirm Its Trailers And Teasers Mostly Featured Very Early Moments From The Game

I’ve played over 135 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. I finished the story and did most of the optional side missions. So trust me when I tell you that the vast majority of the content featured in past GTA 6 trailers, gameplay videos, and teasers comes from the prologue and first two chapters of the game, and there’s a whole lot you haven’t seen yet.

To figure this out, I rewatched the main Grand Theft Auto 6 teasers and trailers released so far by Rockstar, meaning the first trailer, second trailer, extended gameplay trailer, launch trailer, and recently released pre-load trailer. I kept track via a notepad of any time a scene appeared that was from a moment or mission later in the game. Andâthankfully, for fans who don’t want the game spoiled ahead of playing itâI calculated that about 75 percent of what was shown in those past videos comes from the very early chapters of GTA 6.Â

In fact, the game’s first and second trailers show almost entirely very early moments. The extended look and later trailers include a bit more from later missions and cutscenes, but even those trailers are very careful about what they show.

Interestingly, rewatching these trailers after playing GTA 6, IÂ  noticed at least a few examples of Rockstar making changes or edits to cutscenes or missions to remove a character or move a moment to a different location. Rockstar has done this before, so it wasn’t surprising, but it’s something worth noting. If you’ve been trying to piece together GTA 6‘s story from all these trailers, just know that some of what you’ve seen has been tweaked, either to hide spoilers or due to development changes.

Anyway, this is all to say that, no, watching all these trailers over the last few years hasn’t spoiled much in GTA 6. Some early cutscenes and missions might feel familiar to GTA sickos who rewatched all these videos, but there are still some really big and wild surprises and memorable moments left to discover in Grand Theft Auto 6, which is out now on PS5 and Xbox.

#3641. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

In GTA 6 you've got a partner in crime, and it's quite a bit different than it was when you were pulling heists with Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in the last game. Jason and Lucia aren't just criminal associates, they're a couple, and their romantic relationship is a big part of the story.

Jason and Lucia can grow closer or more distant, depending on your actions, behavior, and choices. That goes for everything from story missions to random criminal acts to everyday interactions and activities. Here's how Jason and Lucia's romance works in GTA 6.

There are four levels to Jason and Lucia's relationship that can change depending on how you play and the choices you make, one being the lowest and four being the highest. Here are the levels:

When you begin playing as a couple in Chapter 1, your relationship is already a strong one, though it'll still take a while to get it up to 4/4, if that's your goal. Certain actions, activities, and choices will raise your relationship score, and you'll know you've done it when you hear a chime and see a +♥️ appear on the right side of your screen.

Here are just a few actions that will add a ♥️ to your score, and there are plenty more:

*Note: You can't initiate sex whenever you want, but there are multiple times in GTA 6 when a sex scene is available to you, signified by double hearts over your home icon on the map or with certain limited-time onscreen prompts.

What leads to a sex scene? In my playthrough, twice these scenes happened while I was showering as one of the characters and the other asked if they could join me (and you can decide to let them or not). Another was after I reached a major milestone by contributing money to our savings account (hey, financial security is a major turn-on in real life, too!) and there was also a sex scene after a sizable heist. All of these happened while I was at a 4/4 "Hot Together" relationship status.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

You can also lose hearts from your relationship. This didn't happen often in my playthrough, but here's the ones I experienced:

According to Rockstar, if you want a strong relationship in GTA 6, you have to play both sides of that relationship. That means not just playing as Jason and doing nice things for Lucia, but also playing as Lucia and treating Jason well.

For my playthrough, where I reached the end of the game with a 4/4 "Hot Together" status, my stats show that I played nearly the exact same amount of time as Jason as I did Lucia.

Don't worry, this couple isn't joined at the hip. Both Lucia and Jason have missions, storylines, and activities they can (and are sometimes required to) complete alone. You can play plenty of GTA 6 as just a single character running around without the other, just remember to occasionally spend some time with your partner, respond to their texts, and switch to the other character from time to time.

But trust me, you'll want to spend lots of time together. Their relationship is fun to take part in, from both sides. Plus, doing crimes as a couple really pays off. It's helpful to have an extra set of hands to point guns at people, do crowd control during robberies, shoot out a cop's tires while driving, and carry off more loot than you could handle if you were rolling solo.

I'll be honest: I don't know how the game is different if you have a 4/4 relationship or a 1/4 relationship, because I've only played through the story once at this point, and I kept my relationship as strong as possible for nearly the entire game. We'll know more about the effects of a weak relationship as other players experiment with their relationship status, and we'll update this guide with what we find out.

#3639. Sci-fi RPG Exodus continues evoking Mass Effect by revealing female lead and nicknaming her FemJun

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

There are, however, big and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year."

I absolutely loved Channing Tatum's Gambit in Deadpool & Wolverine. His ridiculous Cajun accent, the way Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool couldn't understand half of what he was saying, and the fact that Tatum finally got to play the character after years of trying made his appearance one of my favorite parts of the movie. But with Gambit returning for Avengers: Doomsday on the 2026 movie schedule, I've been wondering whether Marvel would give him more to do than make everybody laugh. Thankfully, Kevin Feige has some reassuring news.

Speaking with Empire about the upcoming Marvel movie and the return of the original Fox-era X-Men, the Marvel Studios president discussed what audiences can expect from Tatum's Remy LeBeau. And it sounds like the character will have considerably more going on this time around. According to Feige:

He's a standout. It's fun to see Gambit be as charismatic as he was in Deadpool & Wolverine, and yet in Doomsday it's not all for laughs. He's a fully-rounded character.

That's exactly what I was hoping to hear. Don't get me wrong, I laughed every time Gambit opened his mouth in Deadpool & Wolverine. Watching the Merc with the Mouth struggle to decipher his thick accent was hilarious, especially when he asked whether the Minions were his dialect coach. But I also want to see Tatum get a chance to actually play Gambit as a full-fledged character. After all, the mutant hero has quite a bit more going for him than an accent and a deck of exploding playing cards.

In the comics, Remy LeBeau is a former thief with a complicated past, and his relationship with Rogue remains one of the X-Men's most recognizable romances. There's plenty for Marvel to work with. Considering how long Tatum fought to play him, I'd hate to see the character reduced to merely comic relief.

For years, the actor tried to get a standalone Gambit movie made at 20th Century Fox. The project went through numerous delays and creative changes before Disney acquired the studio, and the film was ultimately canceled. Then Ryan Reynolds helped bring Tatum's version of the mutant to life in 2024, finally giving him the opportunity he'd been chasing for the better part of a decade.

Tatum has already said his approach to Gambit would change for Doomsday. He previously explained that directors Anthony and Joe Russo wanted him to dial back the exaggerated Cajun accent, allowing the character to have more serious moments without losing what made his introduction so entertaining.

With that in mind, Feige's latest comments become particularly encouraging. It's one thing to promise a slightly more understandable Gambit, but hearing that Marvel considers him a standout character suggests they're giving the 21 Jump Street star room to explore another side of Remy.

The Gambit-Related Mistake Channing Tatum Nearly Made: ‘It Would’ve Just Been A Catastrophe’

Of course, there's still plenty we don't know about his role in the epic comic book movie. Doomsday is bringing back several familiar X-Men, including James Marsden's Cyclops, Ian McKellen's Magneto and Patrick Stewart's Professor X. Empire also revealed a new look at Gambit alongside Cyclops outside the X-Mansion, which is pretty cool considering Tatum never got to appear alongside the original team during Fox's run. With Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom threatening the multiverse, I imagine there will be plenty of opportunities for Gambit to put those playing cards to work.

I'm excited to see what Tatum does with a character he clearly loves, especially now that he gets another opportunity to play him. Keep the charm, let him crack a few jokes, and maybe give the guy a few standout character moments that audiences won't soon forget. That's not asking too much, is it?

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters Dec. 18. But until then, fans can revisit Gambit's appearance in Deadpool & Wolverine, streaming with a Disney+ subscription.

#3637. Grand Theft Auto 6 Includes A Joke About GTA 7

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6GTA 7Rockstar Games

After a very long wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. And the new game contains a joke that pokes fun at how long it took Rockstar to make GTA 6 and also references the franchise’s past and future.

In GTA 6, players can scroll through Snapmatic, an Instagram-like social media platform found on Jason and Lucia’s in-game phones. Snapmatic contains hundreds and hundreds of posts, videos, and comments. As you play the game, more posts are added as people react to the events of GTA 6 and also just post memes, conspiracies, funny videos, and other random junk.

And very early in the game, if you check Snapmatic, you can find a post complaining that gamers in the world of GTA 6 got a video game based on an in-universe kids’ cartoon before Race and Chase 7.

For those not aware, Race and Chase is a reference to Grand Theft Auto‘s original name. Before the original top-down GTA became what we know today, it started life as a game that would have let players race around as street racers or chase down those drivers as cops. Hence the name Race’n’Chase. As the idea evolved, so did the name.

It seems very likely that Race and Chase 7 is a nod to GTA 7. And the post on Snapmatic joking about getting a Barnyard Blue video game before Race and Chase 7 seems to be Rockstar acknowledging the years of people posting comments online like “I can’t believe we got [insert game sequel/remake/etc] before GTA 6.” Apparently, in the world of GTA 6, gamers have been waiting a long time to play the new Race and Chase. I understand their collective pain.

This isn’t the first time Race and Chase has popped up in a GTA game, either. In GTA Online, players can find and play three variants of an arcade racing game titled Race and Chase. If we assume those are the first three games in the series, then I’d assume that RAC 4 and RAC 5 moved the franchise away from being just a basic arcade racing game and into something big enough to have people super-hyped for Race and Chase 7. Good luck with the wait. Hope it’s worth it.

#3636. ChatGPT's New GIF Generator Is Fun, but Won't Replace Us Humans (Yet)

Khamosh Pathak is a freelance tech journalist with over 13 years of experience writing online. An accounting graduate, he turned his interest in writing and technology into a career. He holds a specialization in user experience design from ISDI Parsons in Mumbai, where he sought to deepen his understanding of UX, consumer devices, and interplay between software and technology.

Khamosh has written thousands of how-tos and guides on every major platform (iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows). He got started writing how-tos and guides for Guiding Tech, where he also published several e-books. His work has also been seen at MakeUseOf, How-To Geek, and PCMag. He is truly passionate about brewing good coffee.

When it comes to generating AI images, both Gemini and ChatGPT do a passable job. In most cases, the results will look AI-generated, but they likely won’t have glaring spelling issues or missing limbs. Now, OpenAI is trying something new, introducing GIF support for ChatGPT. It's the company's first "moving images" feature since OpenAI shut down Sora, and while you can generate hyper-realistic videos in Gemini, this new ChatGPT feature is trying to fill in the gap, in a small way.

OpenAI is pitching the new feature as an animation tool, not exactly as a way to create looping videos—though that’s how I ended up using it. You give ChatGPT a prompt, as detailed as you can make it, and the chatbot produces a GIF in just a few seconds. You can start with your own drawings or images, too. ChatGPT uses sketches as the base for animations, though it can turn any still image into animated GIFs. Like other AI editing tools, you can edit it if ChatGPT didn't quite get it right: You can ask ChatGPT to make the GIF longer or shorter, remove certain objects, change the style, slow down transitions, among other edits.

AI art can be quite sterile, but I was surprised by how adding motion and animation to the mix makes generating images a lot more fun. Unlike traditional GIFs, which usually pull from existing video clips, you can turn anything you want into a GIF, which is especially cool if you're using your own art. In my testing, I found this to be the most rewarding part. It’s not always possible to one-shot a GIF with a single prompt. But after a few rounds of edits, I ended up creating some GIFs that I actually wanted to share in my WhatsApp groups.

That being said, I think human-made GIFs are still the gold standard here. For example, I asked ChatGPT to generate a video of someone brewing a pour-over, with a gooseneck kettle, showing the coffee blooming process. It did okay, but it’s nothing like actually making a pour-over. The kettle doesn’t move in circles, the water doesn’t rise evenly, there are no bubbles, and the steam is all over the place.

Compare that to the GIF below, which comes from a royalty-free video. Even though it’s a compressed, low-quality, and noisy GIF, it still shows the movement of the pour, the water rising, and even the bubbles. The details captured by a real video just aren’t there in ChatGPT GIFs. If that’s what you’re expecting, you will be disappointed. But I don't think that's the point of this feature anyway.

I found that ChatGPT excels when you’re making something fun, and you don’t look into the details too much. It pulled off a loop of a cat playing with a ball, and it was great at making a festive GIF for Diwali. It even made a GIF based on a photo. I asked it to create a fun promotional GIF for my JBL Bluetooth speakers, and it did the job quite well. At first, the transitions were too jarring, and the movement just made no sense. After some editing, though, I got it to a decent place.

Still, the main issue with ChatGPT GIFs is that complex movement and transitions aren’t nailed down. A hand shifts position weirdly between frames, and colors and objects appear out of nowhere. But if you can get over these issues, you can make some fun, lighthearted GIFs and memes to share with your friends on Instagram or WhatsApp.

#3635. PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

12.2 million gamers can be wrong, apparently.

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation users claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

The case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

The lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

It’s no secret that Taylor Swift has amassed a large group of celebrity friends. Selena Gomez, Ed Sheeran and Sabrina Carpenter are just a few of the big names that make up Swift’s personal orbit. The beloved pop star has spoken quite a bit about friendship over the years and, most recently, she spoke about it in reference to her involvement with the 2026 movie schedule entry Toy Story 5. Swift’s latest sentiments on the subject are particularly poignant given where she reportedly stands with Karlie Kloss and Blake Lively.

For the latest Toy Story film, Swift wrote and recorded an original song, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” and it’s currently nominated for two Grammy Awards. Swift has been making the rounds amid awards season, helping the Pixar team promote the legacy sequel, which seems to be a serious contender for some major awards. During a press conference, Swift discussed (via Hello!) the acclaimed movie’s theme of friendship and stressed the importance of someone looking back on such intimate bonds. She also said this:

You may feel, ‘Oh, that friend I had, that was really a special time, and even though I don't know that person anymore, I hope they're doing great,’ or feeling like you could count on your friends to be there when you needed them; feeling like you don't need to have a million of the wrong friends.

The “Delicate” performer’s comments fall directly in line with the narrative of the new Toy Story film, which sees young Bonnie attempting to make genuine friendships. At the same time, cowgirl doll Jessie also reflects fondly on the bond she had with her former owner, Emily. Those plot threads culminated into a truly sentimental third act for the billion-dollar-grossing film. Aside from that, though, Swift’s thoughts are indeed sweet, and they do speak to the nature of how friends come in and out of our lives as time goes on.

Given Swift’s sentiments, it’s honestly hard not to think about her own girl squad and where she stands with certain people. Her relationships with Lively and Kloss have been significant topics of discussion over the past year, and there are a few reasons for that.

We Know Taylor Swift And Travis Kelce Said 'No Gifts' At Their Wedding (But They Did Ask Guests For Something)

The Swift/Kloss friendship began in 2012 after the two publicly showed admiration for each other, and they remained tight until rumors of a falling-out between the two surfaced in 2018., By 2019, it was alleged that Kloss’ continued friendship with former talent manager Scooter Braun (who was in conflict with Swift over her music catalogue) served as a point of contention. While Swift and Kloss wouldn’t be spotted publicly for years after that, the latter surprisingly attended an Eras Tour show. Also, Kloss’ presence at Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in July 2026 and her subsequent attendance at Chiefs games also seemed to suggest the two were friends again.

Meanwhile, Lively and Swift’s friendship seems to be in a very different place. The pair became friends around 2015 and, for years, they were chummy, even attending Chiefs games together. However, the friendship reportedly soured in early 2025 when Swift was pulled into Lively’s It Ends with Us drama with Justin Baldoni. The rumors of a strained friendship seemed to be confirmed when Lively and husband Ryan Reynolds weren’t invited to Swift’s wedding.

Something that should be made clear in all of this, however, is that Taylor Swift hasn’t publicly addressed the states of her relationships with Blake Lively and Karlie Kloss. With that, the general public can only speculate as to where Swift truly stands with these other stars. Regardless, considering how much emphasis Swift places on the importance of friendship – whether that be related to Toy Story 5 or not – I wouldn’t be surprised if fans were to continue to keep eyes on her friend group.
